speaker: R
text: In my town, if your reflection blinks before you do, you have three days left.

speaker: R
text: Nobody knows where those people go. Their beds are made, and their shoes are still by the door.

speaker: R
text: So every morning, my whole family stands at the bathroom mirror and blinks together.

speaker: R
text: Last week, it was Jenny from next door. She told me at recess, and she laughed, like it was a joke.

speaker: R
text: On day three, her bike was still on the lawn, and her house was dark.

speaker: R
text: After that, I started noticing little things.

speaker: R
text: My dad started shaving in the kitchen, with no mirror at all.

speaker: R
text: My mom covered every mirror in the house with towels. She said it was for the dust.

speaker: R
text: And at dinner, my little brother wouldn't look at his spoon.

speaker: R
text: Tonight, I pulled the towel off the bathroom mirror.

speaker: R
text: All three of them came to the doorway behind me.

speaker: R
text: But in the mirror, I was standing there alone.

speaker: R
text: They were never blinking with me. They were watching me blink.

speaker: R
text: And this morning, for the first time, my reflection blinked first.
